subject: Acme Health — model fit, streaming UX & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@acmehealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Thanks — discovery recap + next steps

Hi Liam & Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Goal: Evaluate streaming QA assistant for patient-facing triage with strict latency (<= 200ms token) and stop-sequence safety rules.
- Success metrics discussed: answer accuracy on our 150-case prompt set, partial-output coherence, and 95th percentile latency under 250ms.
- Current blockers: legal wants model provenance + SOC 2 evidence; engineering flagged partial outputs truncating sentences on streaming.

Proposed next steps: 
1) I’ll share a model-fit pack (benchmarks + prompt set) and a sample streaming trace from a similar customer. See attachments: acme_benchmarks_v1.csv, prompt_set_v2.txt.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Jordan and Rishi to review streaming behavior and stop-sequence handling (45 min). Please share 2 windows next week that work.
3) We’ll follow up with a recommended model shortlist + quantization/latency tradeoffs after the deep-dive.

Is that aligned? Any corrections, please reply and I’ll update.

Thanks,
Marissa

Date: 2026-11-29T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Model-fit pack + streaming sample + scheduling

Hi all —

Per our discussion, attached is the initial model-fit pack and a short streaming trace from a production deployment that highlights partial-output behavior: streaming_sample_trace.txt. Highlights below: 

- Recommended models (shortlist):
  * redwood-v1-7b (float16) — best accuracy/latency balance for short medical prompts.
  * redwood-v1-13b-q4_0 — better coherence on longer context, ~1.5x higher cost but fewer regressions on longer answers.
  * open-glm-6b-quant — lowest cost; works well if we enable prefix caching for repeated question types.

- Benchmarks attached (acme_benchmarks_v1.csv): includes top-line accuracy vs. our 150-case prompt set, token latency percentiles, and memory footprint.

- Streaming UX notes:
  * Observed issue: intermittent sentence truncation ~2% of responses at token window boundaries. Root cause often a stop-sequence misalignment or split-token emission when using very short chunk sizes.
  * Quick mitigations: tighten stop-sequence rules on the client-side, increase chunk-size slightly to reduce split-token events, and enable lookahead buffering of 1–2 tokens in the runtime for critical flows.

- Security/compliance: I included high-level provenance notes; our security team can provide SOC 2 artifact links in the deep-dive.

Proposed technical deep-dive windows (PT):
- Tue 2026-12-01 10:00–10:45
- Wed 2026-12-02 13:00–13:45

Liam / Priya: pick a slot and I’ll send calendar invites. Jordan / Rishi / Olga: please review the streaming_sample_trace.txt and acme_benchmarks_v1.csv before the call — we’ll want to propose a short A/B evaluation to validate mitigations.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: acme_benchmarks_v1.csv, streaming_sample_trace.txt, prompt_set_v2.txt

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Model-fit pack + streaming sample + scheduling

Heads-up / internal notes: copying the external thread here for context. Quick take after a first pass on the trace and benchmarks: 

- The truncation looks like classic split-token emissions at chunk boundaries; runtime currently emits every 80ms chunk. For Acme’s latency SLO we should try 120ms chunks with a 2-token lookahead in the runtime — this trades a small latency increase for much higher coherence (we saw partial-output drop from ~2% to ~0.3% in internal tests).
- Stop sequences: their prompt set uses both explicit tokens ("END") and natural-language stops. Recommend we normalize to an explicit token for safety-critical flows and enforce client-side filtering to avoid accidental early stops.
- Eval plan: run A/B (redwood-v1-7b float16 baseline vs redwood-v1-13b-q4_0) across the 150-case prompt set with streaming enabled. Metrics: answer accuracy, partial-output rate, 95th pct latency, token cost.

I can take lead on the A/B evaluation and set up an isolated job on Dedicated for 24 hours. Rishi / Olga — can you confirm resource availability and estimate cost for a short Dedicated run?

— Jordan
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com
